ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended); Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 5895, as amended); Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on the Regulation and Supervision of Designated Business (Act No. 11868, as amended); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 5559, as amended); Regulations on Supervision of Financial Transactions and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Corporate Registration Matters Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry, Competent District Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarize the registry certificate before a Korean notary, then have the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Apostille Section issue an apostille; use directly in Apostille Convention states. Consular Legalization: notarize, have MOFA authenticate the notary certificate, then have the destination-state embassy/consulate in Seoul legalize; never combine apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Tax Clearance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service, Jurisdictional District Tax Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: tax office certificate notarized and apostilled by MOFA. Consular Legalization: notarized certificate authenticated by MOFA and then legalized by the competent destination consulate; the two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa Board of Directors or Founding Incorporators before Formation, and Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarized board resolution or incorporator declaration directly apostilled by MOFA. Consular Legalization: notarized instrument, MOFA authentication, destination consulate legalization; no sequential chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding incorporators of Yuhan Hoesa and the Commercial Registry Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: certified copy from the registry notarized and apostilled by MOFA. Consular Legalization: notarized certified copy, MOFA authentication, destination-state consulate legalization; apostille not used for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Bank maintaining the Yuhan Hoesa operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: bank officer signature notarized and apostilled by MOFA. Consular Legalization: notarized bank letter authenticated by MOFA and then legalized by the embassy/consulate of the destination country; parallel routes only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registered Office and Lease Evidence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Building Owner/Lessor and National Tax Service Registration Record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: lease contract and tax registration statement notarized and apostilled by MOFA. Consular Legalization: notarized documents, MOFA authentication, destination consulate legalization; no hybrid chain.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all individuals and entities associated with the beneficial ownership chain of Yuhan Hoesa, including direct and indirect shareholders, directors, signatories, and counterparties, against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the KoFIU/domestic Korean sanctions and public interest notification lists. PEP screening must follow FATF methodology: proactively monitor senior state officials, leadership in state-owned enterprises, and political party officers, together with their immediate family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence must be documented before bank account opening, generate periodic retest alerts, and require board approval for any positive PEP/designated-risk match; all negative media, source-of-wealth, and transaction monitoring results must be preserved for at least five years under the Specific Financial Transaction Information Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr) and National Tax Service Home Tax System (www.hometax.go.kr) for business registration name confirmation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act, the trade name of Yuhan Hoesa must be written in Hangul as the official Korean name. If a foreign word or corporate designation is used,

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter 4, Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 543 to 613, together with the Commercial Registration Act, as amended; incorporation registration is completed by filing the statutory application with the competent District Court Commercial Registration Division under Article 34 and related procedural and registration rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Registration Office of the competent District Court of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, administered through the Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration System (I-REOS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company (Commercial Registration Act statutory form) together with the Articles of Association and the certificate of capital contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act does not mandate a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Association must fix the total capital and each member's contribution. Every contribution must be fully paid, in cash or kind, before the incorporation registration is filed, and the paid-in amount must be evidenced by a confirmation of deposit issued by a domestic financial institution. Korean law does not require a blocked escrow account; however, funds must be

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service administers border and export controls through UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) under the Commercial Act by registration with the Commercial Registration Court registry. Step 2: File an Application for Business Registration with the district tax office of the principal place of business, including the corporate articles of incorporation, commercial registration certificate, lease evidence, and, if foreign-owned, the foreign investment report filed with the Minister of Economy and Finance / KOTRA Invest Korea under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Step 3: The NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number (taxpayer identification number) and a Business Registration Certificate; this single number covers corporate income tax, value-added tax, and withholding registration. Step 4: For a non-resident foreign entity without a domestic fixed place of business, the foreign entity must appoint a domestic tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes, submit the same registration application through the agent, and obtain a foreign resident tax registration number before making taxable supplies in Korea. Step 5: License-specific registration is separately required for health functional food retailers under Ministry of Food and Drug Safety rules before NTS final recognition is effective.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not have check-the-box pass-through elections; a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a domestic corporation on worldwide income. A 100% domestic subsidiary group may elect consolidated corporate tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act, but that election does not alter the entity-level tax classification or VAT identity of the LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration exemption: every entrepreneur conducting taxable supply in Korea must register from the first supply. KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable supply is the simplified taxpayer (small taxpayer) classification boundary only, not a VAT registration threshold. Foreign non-resident electronic suppliers to Korean consumers must register under the electronic services special VAT treatment before the supply begins and cannot use the KRW 80,000,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: General taxable persons must issue tax invoices electronically through NTS HomeTax or a certified Automated Service Provider API; e-tax invoice data must be transmitted to NTS for validation and storage. Korea does not operate a pre-clearance tax stamp system, but the NTS e-Tax Invoice System assigns acceptance serial numbers, performs matching checks between issuers and VAT returns, and flags anomalies in real time. For B2C sales, the seller must issue a Cash Receipt through the NTS Cash Receipt system when a purchaser requests one, including online pharma/nutraceutical payment rails. An anti-fraud digital audit trail (acceptance numbers, issuer registration, and transaction reconciliation) is mandatory for all cross-border e-commerce export claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 11 of the Value-Added Tax Act if the goods physically leave Korea through legitimate customs export clearance and ownership passes to a non-resident. For nutraceutical e-commerce, the seller must show the product was exported under the seller's exporter declaration, not merely delivered to a domestic forwarding warehouse. Qualifying offshore digital services that are supplied to non-resident users and effectively used outside Korea may also be zero-rated, but the supplements transaction is subject to the physical export rule. The exporter may claim input VAT refunds attributable to zero-rated export sales; the claim must be substantiated with the documents listed below.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export bill of entry) issued by Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill from the ocean/air carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange bank export proceeds confirmation (Foreign Exchange Transaction confirmation) evidencing settlement in foreign currency
Commercial invoice, packing list, and purchase order
Freight forwarder or cargo handler certificate of actual export movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audits export zero-rating by matching customs export declarations, bills of lading, and bank foreign-currency receipt records. If export proceeds are not received within the 180-day statutory foreign-exchange collection period or the export documents are false, the VAT zero-rating is revoked retroactively, uncollected 10% VAT is assessed with statutory interest, and the taxpayer is liable for additional taxes and unfaithful tax invoice penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent customs declarations are punishable under the Customs Act with criminal penalties and fines, and tax evasion referrals to the prosecutor are made under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), operating as the central bank and the designated foreign-exchange reporting authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, together with the Financial Supervisory Service and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit for AML enforcement
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea employs a largely liberalised but notification-heavy exchange-control framework. Current-account payments and receipts are freely convertible for documented trade, service, and dividend flows; no prior BOK approval is required for genuine business transactions executed through registered foreign-exchange banks. Capital-account transfers are regulated: inward direct equity investment must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA/Invest Korea, and outward remittances of invested capital or distributable profits require the foreign-invested company report number, audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and the foreign-exchange bank's transaction screening. A mandatory currency surrender requirement does not exist, but exporters must repatriate proceeds to a domestic foreign-exchange bank within the statutory collection period and evidence the underlying export. Dividend and capital repatriation are permitted once corporate tax and withholding obligations are settled, and every transfer must be transmitted through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Banks also require Real-Name Financial Transaction Act verification for the Korean-won operating account. Undocumented e-commerce merchant receipts routed through third-party platform payment pools face heightened scrutiny and should never be used as substitute treasury inflows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Korea does not impose a fixed percentage conversion-to-won surrender ratio. The statutory collection rule requires export proceeds to be received within six months from the export declaration date, unless the foreign-exchange bank approves an extension for capital goods or project-based supply contracts. The full foreign-currency receipt may then be credited to, and retained in, a domestic foreign currency deposit account without mandatory conversion. All export receipts must be reconciled to the export invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration. For nutraceutical e-commerce sales settled through overseas payment gateways, the platform settlement statements and gateway payout reports must be preserved to prove collection within the period and to support the current-account classification of the revenue.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) and FX Current Account
Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Investment (USD/KRW) plus Trade Services
Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account and RMB/KRW Clearing Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Commercial LC Processing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very Low; not viable as a primary treasury rail. A foreign fintech EMI that is not licensed as a domestic electronic financial transaction provider cannot open a Korean won demand-deposit account, cannot make mandatory FEIS foreign-exchange declarations, cannot issue a compliant Real-Name verified corporate account, and cannot process tax payments, LC issuance, or import-export settlement. Such EMIs may only be used as an ancillary collection access point for international consumer card transactions if the aggregate funds are immediately swept into a domestic licensed-bank account and all platform-settlement detail is available to the bank for transaction monitoring. Using an EMI as the main operating or liquidity account would create unregulated cross-border money flows and trigger likely KoFIU STR filings and bank relationship termination.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch attendance by the statutory director and any signatories is generally mandatory under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and Korean FSS AML guidance; remote e-KYC is normally reserved for Korean nationals utilising accredited non-face-to-face verification. For non-resident beneficial owners and foreign directors, Tier-1 banks require an original passport, seal registration or notarised/apostilled power of attorney, and a live interview with compliance staff at the branch. Remote consular proxy opening is rarely accepted; if the statutory director cannot present in person, the bank may permit a Korean resident officer or local attorney to open the account only after obtaining the director's apostilled POA, CDD questionnaire, passport legalisation, and an independent video call under the bank's internal waiver, but this is discretionary and subject to a longer approval timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore shareholding and opaque ultimate beneficial ownership in a newly formed LLC filing as a licensed nutraceutical e-commerce operator
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles of association, share register, directors' register, signed UBO declaration, source of wealth for each shareholder, 12 months original bank statements showing accumulated wealth, tax residence certificates, reference letters from the precedent banks, and a board resolution approving the Korean AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk product classification for dietary supplements and nutraceuticals, which Korean banks map to fraud and health-claim reputation risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the MFDS health-functional-food business registration or import license, GMP certificates of the manufacturers, product registration/permit documents, certificate of analysis for each batch, customs import declarations, product liability insurance policy, consumer complaint and recall procedure, and legal marketing review showing compliance with Korean functional-food advertising standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border revenue settlement pattern involving offshore payment processors, marketplace stores, and prepaid/card rails creating potential round-tripping or trade-based money laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver executed merchant-of-record agreements, payment gateway reconciliation statements, settlement schedules, acquirer payout reports, shipping/tracking proof for physical goods, export customs declarations, chargeback history, and an audited completion path showing that each cross-border receipt corresponds to a real consumer sale and honest value transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions, adverse media, or prior regulatory hits on directors, shareholders, or trade counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Include independent screening reports from reputable providers, passport copies, local criminal record certificates, confirmation of no past FSS/KoFIU enforcement, a comprehensive tax lien search, court litigation check, directorship history, and a written risk remediation statement explaining any past regulatory or criminal finding and the entity's mitigating controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital must be routed as a direct SWIFT MT103 from the corporate investor's licensed bank into the LLC's Foreign Currency Demand Deposit or Capital Escrow Account held at a Korean foreign-exchange bank. The remittance instructions must include the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) report number obtained through KOTRA/Invest Korea and the purpose code for direct equity participation. Funds must be received before bank accounts are activated; the Korean bank will complete source-of-funds checks and issue a certificate of receipt of foreign exchange. This certificate, together with the FIPA filing and foreign investor's report, constitutes the capital verification required to fund registered share capital and to support future dividend/exit remittance. Third-party funding or aggregate platform proceeds are prohibited for capital-account injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating trade payments, use SWIFT MT103 through the Korean bank for intercompany royalties, supplier settlement, logistics, and tax payments, attaching the invoice, proforma contract, MFDS import or approval certificate if applicable, and a completed FEIS foreign-exchange transaction report. For high-value nutraceutical raw-material purchases, use a confirmed irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700/MT710) with draft terms, quality certificates, and B/L as negotiating documents. For short-cycle or lower-value open-account purchases, documentary collections with documents against payment or documents against acceptance are acceptable, provided the bank has a signed underlying sale/purchase agreement and any required clinical or regulatory evidence. All outbound disbursements must be aligned with the company's stated business plan to avoid current/capital account misclassification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts up to 12 months with licensed foreign-exchange banks, executed only against underlying export or import exposure reflected in invoices and contracts
Plain-vanilla OTC FX options purchased (call/put) to hedge forecast nutraceutical cross-border sales/costs, subject to the FSS underlying-risk ratio limits
Cross-currency swaps (USD/KRW) for intercompany loans or long-term working capital facilities, with the loan agreement, BOK reporting confirmation, and FIPA documentation attached

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where KRW deliverability is not available, generally limited to offshore non-resident structures; not recommended as the primary in-country hedging rail for the LLC

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Financial Statement Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company internal; minutes and accounts kept at the registered office and presented to members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year (by 31 March for a calendar-year entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting or to present financial statements within the statutory window exposes the managing director to an administrative fine up to KRW 10,000,000 (approx. USD 7,600) under the Korean Commercial Act; repeated or wilful non-convenience can constitute grounds for a court-ordered judicial dissolution or the appointment of an inspector.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, audited financial statements (if applicable), and entity-level tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea – jurisdictional local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month following the end of the fiscal year (31 March for a calendar-year entity); no proprietary extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers an administrative surcharge of 10% of the underpaid tax (20% if understatement is grossly negligent or fraudulent), plus a daily late-payment interest of 0.025% of the unpaid amount from the date after the due date until full settlement. Persistent default for more than six months may lead to a seizure of corporate assets; continued delinquency for one or more years may result in the NTS applying for an administrative strike-off of the entity from the corporate tax registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal authority (Si/Gun/Gu) where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the month following the corporate income tax deadline (by 30 April for a calendar-year entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing of the local surtax exposes the entity to a non-filing penalty of 20% of the assessed local tax, plus arrears interest of 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount. Unpaid local taxes can result in a default collection order, revocation of the business license for the online retail scope, and, if left outstanding for more than one year, administrative strike-off of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART/audit-verification system, and concurrently the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the company meets the audit threshold, the auditor must issue the report before the annual general meeting and the company must submit the audit report to the FSS within two weeks after the general meeting; for a calendar-year entity with an AGM on 31 March, the FSS deadline is 14 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the external audit report within the prescribed window results in a fine up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 22,800) and forces the FSS to appoint a statutory auditor at the company's cost. Continued non-submission can lead to criminal referral under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and may jeopardise merchant acquiring licences and the renewal of the high-risk pharmaceutical e-commerce sales permit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance and Refresh of Statutory Registers and Beneficial Ownership Schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office (for physical inspection by members, creditors, and authorities) and the National Tax Service (for the annual shareholder/member schedule in the corporate return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registers must be kept up to date continuously; any share or contribution transfer must be recorded within 30 days of the transfer, and the member confirmation schedule must be closed and appended to the annual corporate income tax return by the corporate tax deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misstatement or failure to maintain the statutory registers carries a negligence fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,800); repeated violations are treated as a breach of the Commercial Act and can support a court order for compliance, removal of the managing director, or an adverse finding in AML/KYC due diligence reviews.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit applies to a Yuhan Hoesa in South Korea under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc. and its Enforcement Decree if any one of the following quantitative criteria is met at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year: (1) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 9,000,000); (2) annual turnover or operating revenue equals or exceeds KRW 20,000,000,000 (approx. USD 15,000,000); (3) the average number of regular employees equals or exceeds 300; or (4) the company is designated as a public-interest or large-scale e-commerce entity by the Financial Supervisory Commission due to high-risk cross-border payment processing. Additionally, even if the company does not exceed the above thresholds, the National Tax Service may order a compulsory audit where cross-border affiliates transact in excess of KRW 5,000,000,000 (approx. USD 3,800,000) or where tax records are inadequate to support the declared revenue from online supplement sales.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements of a Yuhan Hoesa are prepared under the Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) if the entity is subject to a statutory external audit. Non-audited smaller LLCs may apply Korean generally accepted accounting principles for non-public entities (K-GAAP) or the simplified Korean SME accounting standards which are converged with IFRS for SMEs. Where the company uses a high-risk merchant account with international card schemes, the acquiring bank and card network rules may also prescribe additional segment reporting and reconciliation standards, but these are commercial rather than statutory frameworks.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Yuhan Hoesa must maintain at its registered office an up-to-date register of members, directors, charges and minutes. Each transfer or variation in a member's contribution must be recorded in the register within 30 days of the assignment; until such registration the transferee is not recognised as a member for voting or distribution purposes. There is no separate standalone annual UBO filing to the court registry in South Korea. Instead, the annual corporate income tax return must include a comprehensive statement of members and beneficial ownership schedule, which operates as the annual confirmation for tax and commercial law purposes. Where the entity processes card payments or maintains a high-risk merchant account, the monetary authority and acquirer require an annual AML certification identifying each ultimate beneficial owner; any change in beneficial ownership must be notified to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 30 days of the change if the entity is a reporting entity under the Specified Financial Information Act. The shareholder and contribution ledger must be closed for a period of seven days before the annual general meeting to confirm the entitled members.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 3,500 per year for registered office, corporate secretarial compliance, and local filing agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - 45,000 per year for a certified CPA statutory audit, depending on transaction volume, cross-border intercompany balances, and scope of the high-risk supplements e-commerce operation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive schedule under the Corporate Tax Act: 9% on taxable base up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for online nutraceutical retail; statutory incentives include Research and Development tax credits, employment/social insurance credits, facility investment credits, and limited foreign investment zone tax exemptions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; income from regular e-commerce remains subject to the full progressive corporate rate plus a 10% local income tax surcharge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Form 1, 'Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Return') with mandatory attached international transaction schedules; filed electronically through the NTS HomeTax/UTAP portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a calendar-year corporation files one final return, with quarterly interim prepayments based on prior year tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 after a December 31 year-end). The return is deemed timely when filed and tax is paid by the due date; no general extension exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross consideration from online dietary-supplement sales, including high-risk merchant account settlements, credit-card charges, shipping, and ancillary fees, before cost deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter all worldwide sales of the Korean LLC. For non-resident shareholders, this box is not the place of dividend declaration; revenue must be reported in full regardless of how profits will be distributed. Reconcile revenue with credit-card processor settlement reports and chargebacks; unexplained gaps invite penal net-worth reconstruction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inventory purchases, inbound logistics, customs duties, raw materials, direct labor, and direct packaging attributable to the nutraceutical products sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the arm's length principle to any inventory or procurement from a foreign related party. If the seller is a related entity in a no/low-tax jurisdiction, attach TP documentation plus customs and logistics records. If payment is routed through a non-resident intermediary with no substance, the deduction may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less cost of sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that gross profit margins match the tested party's TP profile; an unreasonably low Korean gross profit while foreign related parties receive residual profit will be challenged in a transfer pricing audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, platform commissions, logistics, third-party services, personnel, insurance, and operating overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For fees paid abroad (e.g., overseas marketing, software subscriptions, management fees) assess whether the Korean entity has actually received the benefit; invoice, contracts, foreign tax identification numbers, and service reports must be kept. Otherwise add back the expense and the amount may be deemed a dividend to the non-resident shareholder.
Use this line to benchmark the entity's operating margin against the applicable TP profit-level indicator; the Korean entity should retain profit commensurate with its functional and risk profile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, foreign-exchange gains/losses, dividends received, gains on asset disposals, royalties, and other income and charges outside operating activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest expense on loans from non-resident shareholders is subject to thin-capitalization restrictions (3:1 debt-to-equity ratio generally); ineligible interest is non-deductible and may be re-characterized as dividend or deemed royalty subject to 22% withholding tax. Expense accruals to foreign shell entities must be supported by substance evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions adjusting book income to taxable income, including non-deductible entertainment, penalties, donation limiter, foreign taxes, transfer pricing adjustments, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing upward adjustments to foreign related sales are added back with penal additional tax. The portion of royalties or service fees paid to a related non-resident that lacks beneficial entitlement is non-deductible and is reportable as deemed withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income after all statutory adjustments, reduced by available loss carryforwards and tax-exempt reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards are limited to 15 years (for eligible fiscal years) and must be used in chronological order; no loss attributed to non-resident shareholders may be used to offset unrelated Korean-source digital sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 (Corporate Tax and Local Income Tax Surtax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Progressive corporate tax computed on the tax base, plus 10% local income tax surcharge, less tax credits (foreign tax credit, R&D credit, foreign investment credit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax return must show the national tax and the local surcharge separately; foreign tax credits are limited to the Korean tax applicable on the foreign-source item. Do not apply a credit for foreign withholding on a transaction that is really a bogus deductible payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 (International Transactions and Non-Resident Withholding Disclosures)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach intercompany transaction schedules; report foreign transactions with specially related parties, transfer pricing adjustments, foreign dividends, and non-resident shareholder information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When profit is repatriated as dividends, interest, or royalties, this supporting schedule must record each payee, the amount, applicable treaty article, withholding rate, TRC date, and beneficial ownership certificate. The actual dividend WHT (22% statutory unless treaty-reduced) is declared and paid on the withholding return, not on the corporate income tax return; failure to disclose will nullify the treaty claim and trigger 22% WHT plus penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax under Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; failure to file where no tax is payable carries a flat penalty. Under-reporting carries a 10% additional tax (or 40% for fraudulent/false-return cases), plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022% until paid. Failure to withhold on dividends paid to non-residents attracts a 10% withholding-violation penalty plus daily interest. Intentional evasion is criminally referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; criminal fraud can lead to imprisonment and fines, and the NTS has power to blacklist directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate for cash dividends remitted to a non-resident shareholder: 20% corporate income withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a treaty-reduced dividend rate, the non-resident shareholder must before payment provide the Korean withholding agent with (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the residence state, (ii) a beneficial ownership certificate showing actual entitlement to dividends and no conduit arrangement, (iii) Form for Tax Treaty Withholding Tax Reduction/Exemption (application to the withholding agent), and (iv) a supporting memorandum applying the DTA limitations (including the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI, if applicable). The Korean LLC must retain these documents and, if the NTS challenges, pay the statutory 22% and file a refund/correction within statutory periods; otherwise domestic law outranks the treaty and the excess is final.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border interest and royalties is also 22% (20% national plus 2% local surcharge). Under the relevant Double Tax Agreement, rescued treaty rates commonly apply at 10-15% for interest and royalties where the recipient is the beneficial owner and satisfies TRC, ownership-substance, and Principal Purpose Test documentation; royalties for patents and trademarks may be reduced only after NTS treaty approval.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where intercompany transactions with a foreign related party exceed KRW 10 billion per transaction type in a fiscal year; Master File is mandatory where total intercompany cross-border transactions exceed KRW 50 billion. All reporting entities must disclose transactions with specially related parties in the corporate tax return and maintain contemporaneous TP documentation at lower thresholds upon audit demand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the international tax framework applies substance-over-form, beneficial ownership, and the Principal Purpose Test. A Korean LLC must actually carry on management, employees, premises, board decisions, and economically significant functions (CIGA) in Korea to defend its entitlement to treaty benefits and to avoid re-characterization of royalty/dividend flows by the NTS.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Cross-Border Digital Sales Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing online sales receipts, using personal/offshore merchant accounts or cryptocurrency payments to receive dietary-supplement customers' remittances, understating gross sales, and paying out undeclared profits to non-resident shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS assesses the omitted corporate tax plus local surcharge, imposes 20% non-filing additional tax under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2, 10% under-reporting additional tax under Article 47-3 (increased for serious fraud), daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%, and refers the matter to the public prosecutor's office under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is available when the LLC is abusively used as a cover; directors may be jointly and severally liable under the Commercial Act (Article 401), subjected to civil restitution for unpaid taxes, NTS travel bans/blacklisting for foreign residents, asset seizure, and criminal imprisonment of up to two years (or higher terms for aggravated large-scale fraud) with fines of up to twice the amount of tax evaded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse / Sham Cross-Border Royalties and Management Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, licensing fees, or management fees to a foreign related shell company with no employees, no decision-making capacity, no related CIGA, or to a tax haven entity solely to drain Korean taxable profits without arm's-length benchmarking or TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS re-determines the arm's length amount under Article 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, disallows the excess as a non-deductible expense, imposes 20% additional tax on the unpaid corporate tax, and may apply a 10% penalty for failure to submit TP documentation; if fraudulent, criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act follows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign false intercompany contracts expose themselves to personal liability under the Commercial Act (Article 401) and to criminal charges of aiding and abetting tax evasion; the corporate veil can be pierced where the LLC is functionally a payment conduit for shareholders, resulting in asset garnishment, travel blacklisting, disqualification of directors, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping / No Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Organizing the Korean LLC as a passive shell: no Korean office, no resident directors, no real operations, and minimal capital, solely to use DTA reduced rates on dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident owner, while the actual business decisions and digital e-commerce activities are conducted outside Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty benefits are denied because the recipient is not the beneficial owner or lacks substance under the Principal Purpose Test (OECD MLI and Korean DTA protocols); the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 4-3 empowers NTS to disregard the hybrid arrangement and apply 22% withholding on deemed dividends plus additional tax up to 40% in fraud cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The NTS may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable as the de facto entrepreneurs; secondary liability under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 39 can be imposed on directors that transfer assets or strip the company, and directors face civil restitution, travel bans/blacklisting, criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and imprisonment in severe abuse cases.
